concepts.definition: The engineering Ontology of a designed boundary is its single semantic truth, from which atomic function families and downstream design projections derive.

grounding.quote:
The Ontology is one semantic truth (P1, P6; rc.2 #ontology-projection-law).
These preserve it and do not become independent semantic authorities:

concepts.label: Engineering Ontology

concepts.definition: The smallest parameterised atomic function families that make entity lifecycles logically complete. Their derivation matrix records discovered functionality, entity, atomic function or template, higher-order composition, effect class, required authority and disposition.

grounding.quote: | Discovered functionality | Entity | Atomic function or template | Higher-order composition | Effect class | Required authority | Disposition |

concepts.label: Atomic function family

conditions: The boundary has higher-order behaviour.
concepts.definition: An explicitly named governing composition and effect algebra. Typical categories are unit or lift, sequential composition, parallel or applicative composition, fold or evaluation, retry or recovery, recursion or fixed point, and projection.

grounding.quote:
Where the boundary has higher-order behaviour, the Ontology names the
governing composition and effect algebra. Typical categories include unit
or lift, sequential composition, parallel or applicative composition, fold
or evaluation, retry or recovery, recursion or fixed point, and
projection.

concepts.label: Composition and effect algebra

concepts.definition: An irreducible design relation—atomic function family, identity, authority transition, lifecycle relation, topology, effect, closure law or composition law—that cannot honestly be composed from other accepted atoms while preserving meaning. Prime is a semantic-design property, not a property established by implementation size, naming, typing or independent testability.

grounding.quote:
A Prime semantic atom is one irreducible design relation: an atomic
function family, identity, authority transition, lifecycle relation,
topology, effect, closure law or composition law that cannot be expressed
honestly by composing other accepted atoms while preserving the same
meaning (P3, P1; rc.2 #prime-semantic-atoms-and-universal-domain).

concepts.label: Prime semantic atom

concepts.definition: Review and contraction of the complete candidate semantic-atom family and every proposed realisation projection, including identities, authority transitions, lifecycles, topology, functions, composition laws, effects and closure laws.

grounding.quote:
Prime review evaluates the complete candidate semantic-atom family and
every proposed realisation projection, not only functions, carriers or
each atom in isolation. The family includes every proposed identity,
authority transition, lifecycle relation, topology, function, composition
law, effect and closure law. A function-and-carrier-only pass does not
establish whole-family Prime

concepts.label: Whole-family Prime contraction

concepts.definition: A downstream implementation or design unit projecting accepted semantic atoms. Prime-conformance applies to functions, classes, carrier types, top-level schema records and modules; other Ontology projections include diagrams, matrices, IACS, APIs, operation registers, SDK/CLI surfaces, schemas, codecs, manifests, catalogues, target architecture and test/proof inventories.

grounding.quote:
Prime-conformance applies to these realisation projections: functions,
classes, carrier types, top-level schema records and modules. Typed
closure by itself is not sufficient reason to create a new top-level type.

concepts.label: Realisation projection

concepts.definition: The Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set is the smallest lawful top-level carrier family carrying a boundary's real functionality and authority flow. It is the declared carrier inventory to which the cited assurance rules bind conformance tests and unit proof. Example roles include source truth, admission, execution, yielded/recovery, effect plan and public projection carriers.

grounding.quote:
Examples of irreducible architectural carrier roles (P3) include the source
truth carrier, admission carrier, execution carrier, yielded or recovery
carrier, effect plan carrier and public projection carrier.

- Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set (IACS): the smallest lawful
  top-level carrier family required for one boundary;

concepts.label: Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set

concepts.definition: Payload detail inside a boundary that is not top-level by default.

grounding.quote:
- Subordinate Payload: payload detail that exists inside that boundary but
  is not top-level by default;

concepts.label: Subordinate Payload

concepts.definition: The explicit architectural-boundary test a Subordinate Payload must pass before becoming a top-level type, including class, dataclass, TypedDict, enum or named schema record.

grounding.quote:
A top-level class, dataclass, TypedDict, enum or named schema record
justifies its existence as an architectural boundary, not merely as
payload detail (P3, P2; rc.2 #5b-promotion-test). A Subordinate Payload may
be promoted to a top-level type only when at least one of these is true:

concepts.label: Promotion Test

concepts.definition: Design debt in which subordinate payload detail becomes extra peer types without irreducible need: typing discomfort drives promotion, internal records become public without a new authoritative boundary, near-identical top-level types multiply where one family suffices, or one migration silently becomes parallel schema migrations.

grounding.quote:
Boundary Inflation exists when payload detail is promoted into peer types
because the code feels hard to type; internal records are turned into
public schema surface without a new authoritative boundary; many
near-identical top-level types appear for one boundary where one carrier
family would suffice; or one migration ticket silently becomes several
parallel schema migrations. Boundary Inflation is design debt, not
progress (P2).

concepts.label: Boundary Inflation

conditions: A realisation derives from an existing design line, released tenant or reference implementation.
concepts.definition: An explicit derivation chain from constitutional WHAT through reference design, target Ontology and reference-to-Ontology mapping, target design mapping, target module boundary assets and implementation.

grounding.quote:
The required derivation
evidence is: (1) constitutional WHAT; (2) reference design; (3) target
Ontology and reference-to-Ontology mapping; (4) target design mapping; (5)
target module boundary assets; (6) implementation.

concepts.label: Reference-derived module design

concepts.definition: One complete design asset containing distinct domain, execution and lifecycle views, normally Mermaid classDiagram, sequenceDiagram and stateDiagram-v2. These fidelity-checked Ontology projections jointly form the sign-off surface for identity, authority, behaviour, lifecycle and axiom conformance.
exceptions: A project may ratify another text-native format preserving the three distinct views and cross-view checks.

grounding.quote:
The views are not decorative and are not peer truth surfaces: they
are fidelity-checked projections of the accepted Ontology, and together
the sign-off surface for domain identity, authority, behaviour, lifecycle
and axiom conformance (P1, P6).

concepts.label: Three-view design asset

concepts.definition: Durable design reasoning state that, together with the selected method basis, supports reconstruction of governing relations for a declared bounded action and its causally closed affected set. It is carried by existing Ontology evidence, matrices, frame declaration, views and module mapping rather than a separate documentation package.

grounding.quote:
The evidence above is not a documentation deliverable. It is the durable
reasoning state a bounded actor needs, because the actor selecting a local
action generally does not hold the reasoning that produced the governing
frames. Dialogue, commentary, prior-agent memory and implementation
folklore are not that state

concepts.label: Invariant reconstruction sufficiency

concepts.definition: Source-defined action/relation decisions: preserves, changes, duplicates and violates. Their core values concern only the predicate that the action is admissible in the acting frame on the current governing basis.

grounding.quote:
The four decisions are a refinement of the core result algebra
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results)). They answer what the
action does to one governing relation, and each maps to exactly one core
value for the predicate "the action is admissible in the acting frame on
the current governing basis"; the value travels with that predicate and
with the decision, whose meaning stays here

concepts.label: Action-to-relation decisions

concepts.definition: The structural domain projection of the Ontology, normally expressed as classDiagram.

grounding.quote:
The `classDiagram` is the structural domain projection of the Ontology
(P1, P3; rc.2 #domain-model).

concepts.label: Domain model

concepts.definition: The behavioural projection of Ontology functions and authority, normally expressed as sequenceDiagram.

grounding.quote:
The `sequenceDiagram` is the behavioural projection of Ontology functions
and authority

concepts.label: Sequence model

concepts.definition: The lifecycle projection of Ontology entities, normally expressed as stateDiagram-v2.

grounding.quote:
The `stateDiagram-v2` is the lifecycle projection of Ontology entities
(P3, P5; rc.2 #state-model).

concepts.label: State model

concepts.definition: Assessment of product, graph, language, runtime, handler and module axioms across Ontology, authority, domain, sequence, state, native enforcement and admission/compiler evidence, with Verdict and Gap owner columns. Its source-defined verdicts are pass, fail and reasoned not_applicable; undecided evaluations can instead record direct core values.

grounding.quote: | Axiom | Ontology evidence | Authority | Domain evidence | Sequence evidence | State evidence | Native enforcement | Admission/compiler enforcement | Verdict | Gap owner |

concepts.label: Cross-view axiom evaluation

concepts.definition: Separate Ontology and design-pack acceptance decisions owned by the design authority. accepted denotes the accept disposition and maps to satisfied for the candidate's acceptance at its declared design-gate boundary; it is not an assessment result or an artifact-production result.

grounding.quote:
`accepted` is the disposition
`accept`, which maps to `satisfied` for "the candidate is accepted at its
declared boundary", the candidate being the Ontology or the design pack
and the boundary the design gate. A verdict that is not `accepted` is one
of the other three dispositions, mapped there, or no disposition yet,
which is no acceptance result.

concepts.label: Ontology and design acceptance

concepts.definition: A subordinate projection exposing abstract data types, identity/key structures, algorithms, algebraic laws, mutation/effect boundaries, selected implementations and domain-to-computational mappings. It reveals repeated machinery that domain views can conceal, but cannot decide semantic identity, ownership or authority.

grounding.quote:
At a material semantic boundary, the design projects the
domain design into its computational realisation: abstract data types,
identity and key structures, algorithms, algebraic laws, mutation and
effect boundaries, selected implementations, and domain-to-computational
mappings. The cross-view evaluation extends to prove that the domain views
and this projection describe one system

concepts.label: Computational realisation projection

concepts.definition: The explicit semantic and operational roles assigned by design authority to each material realisation component. Multiple roles are lawful; technological capability alone confers no authority.

grounding.quote:
A component's declared role set is design authority;
where a role carries authority, composition and use preserve the
applicable authority relation under IDENTITY §6, which is supporting law
here rather than the owner of the role model (P6). A component may
lawfully hold several roles.

concepts.label: Component role set

concepts.definition: An optional theoretical framing in which a Markov object is a candidate identity-bearing cut: a stable self-bounding pattern with an effective blanket separating identity-bearing from context-bearing aspects. IACS, promotion, boundary inflation and strong boundary typing receive software-design analogies, not added prerequisites.

grounding.quote:
It treats a Markov object
as a candidate identity-bearing cut: a stable self-bounding pattern whose
effective blanket separates what is load-bearing for identity from what is
load-bearing for context.

concepts.label: Markov-object theoretical framing

conditions: This profile governs the realisation boundary.
concepts.definition: Recommended role taxonomy: carrier modules define typed immutable contracts and values; semantic kernels transform carriers without effects; effect shells perform external effects; projection modules derive views from source truth; binding/adapters translate boundaries without inventing law; constructor/materialisation modules produce artifacts from admitted carriers and explicit plans. Modules bound reasoning, expose ownership/consumption/emission/proof and make recurrence visible.
concepts.label: Module role taxonomy

concepts.definition: Typed values carrying source truth, preferably immutable, produced by constructors/parsers, transformed into new carriers or closed results and read by projections.
exceptions: Materially necessary mutation may be justified.

grounding.quote:
Source truth should be carried in typed immutable values unless mutation
is materially necessary (P3, P4b; rc.2 #7-immutable-carrier-rule). The
preferred shape: a constructor or parser produces a typed carrier;
transforms consume one carrier and return another carrier or a closed
result; projections read those carriers without mutating them.

concepts.label: Typed carrier

concepts.definition: Semantic-function outcomes are Product domain values, including unsupported or rejected outcomes; they are distinct from this method's core evaluation results. An evaluation consuming Product outcomes produces its own core value.

grounding.quote:
The outcome values a
semantic function returns are the Product's domain values, not results of
this method; an evaluation that consumes them returns its own core value

concepts.label: Product semantic-function outcome

concepts.definition: An explicit effect boundary, typically file writes, network calls, subprocess execution, event append, manifest publication, prompt delivery or database mutation.

grounding.quote:
Typical effect edges include file writes, network calls, subprocess
execution, event append, manifest publication, prompt delivery and
database mutation.

concepts.label: Effect edge

concepts.definition: A hidden semantic centre is a controller, manager, service method, loop or wrapper whose implementation must be read to discover closure, identity, failure, next work or current truth. Interface bleed is authority leaking between interface families through truth reconstruction, projection-as-closure, report/prompt-as-admission, wrapper decisions or meaning-inventing adapters.

grounding.quote:
A
module is acting as an unlawful semantic centre when reviewers have to
read it to discover what counts as closure, what identity means, what
failure means, what work is next, or what the current truth is. Those
meanings should already exist in carriers, contracts or explicit design
modules.

Interface bleed exists when one
interface reconstructs another interface's source truth; projection logic
becomes closure logic; report or prompt logic becomes admission logic;
public wrappers decide kernel semantics; or adapters invent meaning instead
of translating boundaries.

concepts.label: Hidden semantic centre and interface bleed

conditions: A boundary governs, observes, routes, audits or evaluates another actor, executor, builder or substrate.
concepts.definition: Governance publishes state, structure, unmet pressure or unresolved identities, route eligibility, lawful edit/proof frontier, admitted policy identity and continuity. Strategy prescribes how another actor does work.
exceptions: Strategy ownership may be explicitly included in the boundary's ratified responsibility.

grounding.quote:
Lawful governance publication
includes current state, preserved structure, unmet pressure or unresolved
identities, route eligibility, the lawful edit or proof frontier, admitted
policy identity, and prior-turn or prior-run continuity.

concepts.label: Governance and strategy separation

conditions: The realisation boundary is lawfully open for migration, refactor or bounded implementation.
concepts.definition: Improvement local to the active design/module boundary that preserves declared behaviour, ownership of truth, visibility and effects. It is subordinate to constitutional truth, declared module ownership and functional equivalence.

grounding.quote:
Opportunistic
optimisation is lawful only when it is boundary-local to the active design
or module surface; behaviour-preserving at the declared semantic boundary;
authority-neutral, with no change to ownership of truth;
visibility-neutral, with no silent promotion of subordinate payloads; and
effect-neutral, with no hidden expansion of runtime, persistence or
bootstrap doctrine.

concepts.label: Opportunistic optimisation

conditions: The same realisation pattern occurs across more than one processed boundary.
concepts.definition: A commonisation candidate rather than another purely local clean-up. Candidates are usually non-product truth, authority-neutral, repeated across at least two tickets/modules and usable through local adapters without changing ownership; examples include expectation derivation, nested contract/policy carriers, proof fixtures, effect plans and non-semantic constructor helpers.

grounding.quote:
A recurrence candidate is usually not
product truth, authority-neutral, reused across two or more tickets or
module boundaries, and consumable through local adapters without changing
semantic ownership. Typical candidates include expectation derivation;
nested contract or policy carriers; proof-helper or fixture shaping;
effect-edge request or plan shaping; and constructor or materialisation
helpers that do not own semantic law.

concepts.label: Recurrence extraction and commonisation

conditions: A ticket applies this profile and claims its boundary has been processed.
concepts.definition: A bounded check against the accepted design and exact closure claim, reconstructing the complete selected function from requirements through Ontology, Prime atoms, IACS, views, modules, implementation and module-owned proof. Its subject is the claim's causal closure, not the whole Product or construction history.

grounding.quote:
The complete selected function is the causal closure of the declared
claim, not the whole Product or the whole history of its construction.

concepts.label: Post-ticket bounded design review

concepts.definition: A new-looking interface forwarding to old authority, reconstructing missing truth from it, keeping it executable behind a new name or maintaining green proofs while old law still governs. Such substitution is bridge debt; intentionally retained compatibility is a separate bounded feature.

grounding.quote:
A proxy interface is a new-looking surface that
forwards to the old authority path, reconstructs missing truth from the
old path, keeps the old path executable behind a new name, or allows
proofs to stay green while the old law still governs. This is bridge debt,
not progress. If compatibility is intentionally retained, it is treated as
an explicit feature with its own bounded authority and proof;

concepts.label: Proxy interface

concepts.definition: The subject's DESIGN_MODULE profile: a preferred realisation discipline for Ontology-first derivation, low coupling, authority/effect management and non-bleeding interfaces. Its engineering requirements are distinct from constitutional process, graph-native product law, release decisions and optional theoretical framing.

grounding.quote:
this profile what is
the preferred implementation design discipline when you want
Ontology-first derivation, low coupling, no interface bleed, and explicit
authority and effect management; and the UX profile the additional
discipline that applies when a module realises a UI surface.

concepts.label: DESIGN_MODULE profile

concepts.definition: The profile's review instruments: provenance-supported prompt clauses, 56 design review questions, a functional-realisation checklist and a compact hard gate. Questions and checks describe review obligations; they are not evidence that any implementation passed.

grounding.quote:
When reviewing code under this profile, ask (P6;
rc.2 #14-design-review-questions):

When a project claims functional bias, pure transforms, immutable
carriers, single-owner truth or low-coupling realisation, review
explicitly checks (P6, P5;
rc.2 #14a-functional-realization-review-checklist):

concepts.label: Design review instruments

conditions: Consumer-bound realisation of the ABG role under the graph-execution profile.
concepts.definition: Default identity generators, validators and normalisers for that realisation's own runtime surfaces and the default ODD surface kinds used by default F_D helpers.

grounding.quote:
A consumer-bound realisation of the ABG role under the graph-execution
profile may publish default identity generators, validators and
normalisers for its own runtime surfaces and for the default ODD surface
kinds used by default `F_D` helpers; the permission is scoped to that role
and does not extend to other runtime realisations

concepts.label: Bound runtime identity defaults

concepts.definition: A provenance ledger claiming conservation, replacement or addition of predecessor DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD and one IDENTITY_METHOD row. Routes identify receiving loci; they are provenance only. The ledger also records terminology generalisations, preserved modal force, new result mappings and proposed replacements pending Product-owner acceptance.

grounding.quote:
Rows of rc.2 DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md received by this member, and the one
IDENTITY_METHOD row it closes. Anchors are into rc.2
DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md unless the row names IDENTITY_METHOD; a locus is a
section of this file unless another member is named. Every conserved row
is restated in the receiving member's own text; a route is provenance
only.

concepts.label: Source-disposition provenance ledger

concepts.definition: The subject's Tier-1 EVALUATION member owns claim justification and acceptance, evidence, independent assessment, review results, realisation conformance/equivalence, frame and method qualification, and actual-use evidence of adequate attention. It consumes FOUNDATIONS core results and defines no result values itself.

grounding.quote:
Tier 1. Owns how claims are justified and accepted: claims, evidence,
independent assessment, review results, acceptance, conformance of
realisations and the equivalence ladder, the qualification of frames and
of the method itself, and actual-use evidence of adequate attention.
Consumes [FOUNDATIONS](FOUNDATIONS.md), whose
[Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results) own the core result values this member
uses; it defines no result values of its own.

concepts.label: EVALUATION member

concepts.definition: A load-bearing claim specifies its exact subject, property, governing basis, witness-to-claim relation, nearest excluded weaker property and falsifier before witness selection. An assurance surface is a checker, validator, harness, reviewer or other surface supporting promotion or closure.

grounding.quote:
A load-bearing claim names its exact subject, the property claimed, the
governing basis, the relation between witness and claim, the nearest weaker
property it excludes, and its falsifier, before a witness is selected.
Without these it is evidence discovery, not proof.

concepts.label: Load-bearing claim

grounding.quote:
Every row is one of: derived through an admitted atomic function; derived
through a declared higher-order composition; deferred with an owner and
re-entry condition; excluded by current product authority; or unresolved
as a named gap (P5, P6).

constraints.statement: Every functionality row has exactly one of the five stated dispositions: admitted atomic derivation, declared higher-order derivation, deferral with owner and re-entry condition, exclusion by current Product authority, or named unresolved gap. Variation only in entity/projection/transition kind, policy or subordinate payload should normally be a typed parameter or closed variant of one family rather than a peer function. Where higher-order behaviour exists, design states applicable identity, closure, associativity, cardinality, effect and authority-conservation laws explicitly rather than hiding them in controller flow.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced foundations and P commitments are not fully supplied.

conditions: Discovery or implementation would cross an affected unresolved, contradictory or materially non-equivalent relation.
exceptions: When co_evolution_admissible(B) holds, composition, effects and implementation may be discovered iteratively; Ontology, carrier evidence, implementation and tests may develop together.

grounding.quote:
Composition, effects and implementation may be discovered iteratively only
when `co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds. Otherwise only a disposable spike
may supply evidence across the affected unresolved, contradictory or
materially non-equivalent relation before its design is accepted. Every
retained result is reconciled into accepted design before promotion or
design-method closure. No private helper, loop, adapter or endpoint may
become an undeclared constructor (P6, P2).

Under design-gated sequencing, the
affected unresolved, contradictory or materially non-equivalent relation is
accepted before retained implementation establishes it (P6, P2; §5).

constraints.statement: Absent the stated co-evolution condition, only a disposable spike may supply pre-acceptance evidence across the affected relation; retained implementation waits for relation acceptance. Every retained result must reconcile to accepted design before promotion or design-method closure. Implementation may reveal missing meaning but cannot self-ratify it, and no private helper, loop, adapter or endpoint may become an undeclared constructor.
constraints.uncertainty: The definition of co_evolution_admissible(B) is outside the supplied sections.

exceptions: An out-of-domain case may justify proposing another candidate atom for design admission.

grounding.quote:
Every accepted Prime atom declares the admitted domain over which its law
holds, and within that domain it governs every admitted instance. A later
use case composes or parameterises the atom; it does not fork, shadow,
specialise or reinterpret the atom locally. An out-of-domain case may
justify proposing another candidate atom for design admission. An
in-domain counterexample falsifies the shared atom and re-enters at that
atom's design boundary rather than authorising a feature-local replacement
(P3, P6). An atom without a declared admitted domain remains a candidate
atom; it cannot supply Prime acceptance or Prime-conformance to a
realisation projection.

constraints.statement: Every accepted atom declares its admitted domain and governs every admitted instance. Later uses compose or parameterise it, never locally fork, shadow, specialise or reinterpret it. An in-domain counterexample falsifies the shared atom and requires re-entry at its design boundary. Without a declared domain an atom remains a candidate and supplies neither Prime acceptance nor projection conformance. Atom/unit mappings may be many-to-many only when explicit and free of rival meaning or authority. Atomic functions are not proven Prime until the complete candidate family is contracted; smallness, typing, naming and independent testability are insufficient.

conditions: Before promotion.

grounding.quote:
- can several proposed operations be typed parameters of one atomic
  function?
- are several commands lifecycle transitions over one entity?
- are several reads projections over one source truth?
- are several implementations applications of one higher-order function?
- does the candidate introduce independent identity, authority, effect,
  lifecycle, reuse or public pattern-match semantics?
- has every candidate atom kind entered the same contraction?
- does every realisation unit map explicitly to its accepted atom or
  atoms?
- does any realisation projection introduce, duplicate or reinterpret
  meaning or authority?

constraints.statement: Review covers all candidate atom kinds and projections, asking whether operations collapse to parameters, commands to entity transitions, reads to one truth's projections, and implementations to higher-order applications; whether candidates add independent identity, authority, effect, lifecycle, reuse or public pattern-match semantics; whether every kind entered contraction; whether every unit maps to accepted atoms; and whether projections introduce, duplicate or reinterpret meaning or authority. Individually plausible functions are not Prime if one parameterised template with closed variants carries the same meaning and authority. Visible recurrence is contracted during design; post-implementation recurrence review cannot replace this pass.

conditions: At a material semantic boundary.
exceptions: Work inside an accepted boundary cites the existing Prime basis instead of recreating it.

grounding.quote:
Contraction preserves root authority and every retained semantic relation.
Reducing files, functions, operations or authoring surfaces cannot
compensate for introducing another authority source or truth path (P6,
P4b). Prime evidence states the complete candidate semantic-atom family;
each atom's stable identity, irreducible relation, admitted domain and
falsification condition; the whole-family contraction relation; retained
meaning and authority before and after contraction; accepted loss; and the
explicit total mapping from every proposed realisation projection to its
accepted atom or atoms (P4b, FOUNDATIONS §4 Conservation accounting). Work
inside an accepted boundary cites the existing Prime basis rather than
recreating it (P2).

constraints.statement: Contract each candidate atom, then the resulting whole family. Local irreducibility or unit conformance does not prove global Prime when identity, authority, function, lifecycle, topology, effect or projection meaning is duplicated. Preserve root authority and every retained semantic relation; fewer files/functions/operations/surfaces cannot compensate for new authority sources or truth paths. Evidence states the complete family; each atom's stable identity, irreducible relation, domain and falsifier; contraction relation; before/after meaning and authority; accepted loss; and a total explicit mapping from every proposed realisation projection to accepted atoms.

exceptions: Target design may add structural HOW absent from the Ontology without originating rival meaning.
Implementation branches and test expectations need preserve Ontology meaning but need not be enumerated by the Ontology.

grounding.quote:
If a public operation, sequence message, state transition, carrier or
effect cannot be traced through accepted design to the accepted Ontology,
it is ungrounded design and does not enter the active product line. An
implementation branch or test expectation traces to requirements plus
accepted design; it preserves, but need not be enumerated by, the
Ontology (P6; SPEC_METHOD §2 Trace closure and anti-drift).

constraints.statement: Every design projection identifies its Ontology source and preserved identity, relationship, lifecycle, authority, function or effect law. Intentional omission or flattening declares accepted loss and a failure condition. Projections are not independent semantic authorities. Implementation and tests trace through accepted design, with requirements for branches/expectations. Public operations, sequence messages, state transitions, carriers and effects lacking the accepted-design-to-Ontology trace are ungrounded and excluded from the active Product line.

grounding.quote:
A top-level realisation unit is Prime-conformant only when it projects one
or more accepted Prime atoms without introducing, duplicating or
reinterpreting semantic authority. A topological or effect boundary is
first derived and accepted as a Prime atom. Source-code size and
one-to-one correspondence with an atom are immaterial (P3, P6).

constraints.statement: Derive atoms from the logically complete candidate Ontology before proposing top-level units; whole-family Prime contributes to acceptance of the Ontology basis. Target design, IACS, modules, functions, schemas and tests project accepted atoms rather than originate Prime meaning. Top-level conformance requires projection of one or more accepted atoms without introducing, duplicating or reinterpreting authority; topological/effect boundaries are first accepted atoms. Typical lawful reasons are new admitted graph topology/branch, typed carrier transformation, effect boundary, validation/admission boundary or projection boundary. Typed closure alone, source size and one-to-one correspondence are insufficient or immaterial.

conditions: A unit exists only for one of the listed convenience purposes.

grounding.quote:
A realisation unit is
not Prime-conformant when it exists only to: shorten a call site without
creating a new semantic boundary; aggregate unrelated behaviour for
convenience; preserve an old interface behind a new name; shuttle data
through one more wrapper layer; hide mutation, fallback or orchestration
that should remain explicit; name one more payload variation that carries
no independent authority; turn internal record detail into public schema
surface without an irreducible boundary; mirror another top-level carrier
with only small field variation; or respond to typing discomfort by
multiplying peer classes instead of closing one governing carrier family
(P3, P2).

constraints.statement: The listed convenience-only units are not Prime-conformant: shortened call sites without boundaries; unrelated aggregation; renamed old interfaces; extra data-shuttling wrappers; hidden mutation/fallback/orchestration; payload variants without authority; public internal detail without irreducibility; cosmetically varied carrier mirrors; or multiplied peer classes for typing comfort. The source recommends composition, existing lawful functions and fewer sharper boundaries/carrier families; its purpose is preventing semantic fragmentation and helper sprawl, not minimising lines.

grounding.quote:
Prime review accounts for
governance cost as well as implementation count: contraction is not
successful when it increases authority centres, maintained truth surfaces,
acceptance boundaries, dependency cycles, manually reconciled projections
or review burden. Evidence remains proportional to semantic change and
risk; this rule does not require one artifact or review per concern.

constraints.statement: Review cuts, realisation units, runtime modules and work items are distinct boundaries permitting many-to-one and one-to-many relationships; administrative convenience does not force one-to-one decomposition. Prime contraction accounts for governance cost, and is unsuccessful if it increases authority centres, maintained truth surfaces, acceptance boundaries, dependency cycles, manual projection reconciliation or review burden. Evidence is proportional to semantic change and risk, without an artifact or review per concern. ACTIVATION §6 owns the ambiguity-removed versus reasoning-complexity relation applied here.
constraints.uncertainty: The proportionality relation's full definition is not supplied.

conditions: Defining a schema, carrier family or typed public boundary.
constraints.statement: Derive IACS from accepted Ontology before naming subordinate payloads or implementation modules; it should be named before helper results/internal detail. Required evidence cites accepted Ontology and function derivation, declares the set, maps every carrier to its Ontology law, distinguishes authoritative/downstream roles, defaults all other shapes to subordinate, keeps them private unless promoted, and reconciles implementation before closure. Branch payloads, persistence detail, read-model rows and typing-only field groupings do not automatically justify top-level carriers. IACS neither replaces Ontology nor originates entity/function/lifecycle/authority meaning. Missing declared accepted Ontology or IACS means the schema is not design-method complete; both must be accepted and implementation reconciled before promotion/closure.
constraints.uncertainty: The cited ASSURANCE §§2,7,15 binding and member-head declaration are not supplied.

conditions: A carrier is added, removed, merged or split.

grounding.quote:
- re-derives the complete IACS and classifies every addition, removal,
  merge and split;
- reruns the Promotion Test and the Boundary Inflation prohibition over
  the full revised set, not only newly introduced carriers;
- updates every conformance or checker subject to the declared composite
  carrier relation under the assurance-boundary congruence law of
  EVALUATION §1 (with its freeze and revision in §3); and
- reconciles implementation to the revised set before promotion or
  closure.

constraints.statement: IACS is not numerically frozen: revision is lawful through accepted Ontology/design re-entry. Every revision re-derives the complete set and classifies all changes, reruns Promotion Test and inflation checks over the entire revised set, updates every assurance/checker subject to the declared composite relation, and reconciles implementation before promotion/closure. A prohibition without a lawful revision path is false; revision is also false if gates inspect only new carriers, assurance retains weaker/obsolete subjects, or reconciliation is missing before closure.
constraints.uncertainty: EVALUATION §1 is supplied; §3 freeze/revision law is not.

conditions: Considering promotion to a top-level type.

grounding.quote:
Default
rule: if a shape does not need independent authority, independent reuse or
direct pattern-match semantics, it remains a Subordinate Payload and stays
nested, private or local to the carrier family. The burden of proof is on
promotion; designers and reviewers should assume a candidate type stays
subordinate until an irreducible boundary is shown (P3, P6).

constraints.statement: Promotion requires at least one stated ground: authoritative source carrier; public/persisted contract boundary; explicit public outcome variant directly pattern-matched by consumers; reuse across several modules without semantic bleed; or independent versioning/publication/admission. Promotion is unlawful for mere internal detail of a larger carrier, a once-used local field group, temporary open-dictionary typing shim, private payload variation never crossing a true interface, or cosmetic/local-field mirror. Without need for independent authority, reuse or direct pattern matching, the shape stays nested/private/local. Proof burden is on promotion; designers/reviewers should presume subordination until an irreducible boundary is shown.

conditions: Schema work, including a schema or ticket listing a wide family of types.

grounding.quote:
Schema work declares the IACS, which types are authoritative, which types
are downstream projections, which shapes are Subordinate Payloads, and
which Subordinate Payloads are intentionally deferred from promotion (P3,
P2; rc.2 #5c-boundary-inflation-prohibition). The rule exists to stop type
proliferation from turning one migration into many parallel schema
migrations. If a schema or ticket lists a wide family of types, it
distinguishes the IACS from the Subordinate Payloads; failing to make that
distinction is design drift. Typed closure does not excuse Boundary
Inflation.

constraints.statement: Declare IACS, authoritative types, downstream projections, subordinate shapes and intentional deferrals from promotion. Wide type inventories must distinguish IACS from subordinate payloads; omission is design drift. Typed closure does not excuse inflation or parallel migration proliferation.

conditions: Derivation from an existing design line, released tenant or reference implementation.

grounding.quote:
The minimum lawful design assets for a reference-derived module boundary
are: the named reference design surfaces being used as source material;
the accepted target Ontology, including the disposition of reference
entities, functions, lifecycle, authority, effects and projections; the
target design surfaces that replace or bind those source surfaces; an
explicit mapping that says what is preserved, reshaped, deferred or
demoted to delivery binding in the target line; and the target module
boundary assets required by this profile, including the Ontology-derived
IACS and the three-view design asset (§7) (P6, P4b).

constraints.statement: Code comparison alone cannot establish completion. Minimum assets name reference design surfaces; accepted target Ontology with dispositions for reference entities/functions/lifecycles/authority/effects/projections; replacing/binding target surfaces; explicit preserved/reshaped/deferred/delivery-binding mappings; and target module assets including Ontology-derived IACS and three views. The target boundary must show the derivation chain rather than inherit incidental code drift, delivery quirks, helper sprawl or authority paths; otherwise it is not design-method complete.

conditions: Every new or materially changed semantic or typed module boundary.
exceptions: Unchanged boundaries cite their accepted basis; local realisation work without material semantic-boundary delta does not recreate the gate.
Co-evolution before the gate is allowed only when co_evolution_admissible(B) holds.

Every new or materially changed semantic or typed module boundary carries
one accepted Ontology and one complete three-view Mermaid design asset
before the boundary is promoted or claims design-method closure (P6, P1;
rc.2 #5e-ontology-and-three-view-behavioral-design-gate). When
`co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds, design evidence, implementation and
tests may develop together before that gate; otherwise the affected
unresolved, contradictory or materially non-equivalent relation is
accepted before retained implementation establishes it. Unchanged
boundaries cite their accepted basis; local realisation work with no
material semantic-boundary delta does not recreate this gate (P2).

constraints.statement: Before promotion or design-method closure the boundary carries one accepted Ontology and one complete three-view design asset. Without admissible co-evolution the affected unresolved, contradictory or materially non-equivalent relation is accepted before retained implementation establishes it. A broad flowchart cannot replace the three models.

conditions: An active boundary's design asset.
exceptions: The accepted Ontology may be a boundary-bounded slice of a wider accepted Product Ontology.

grounding.quote:
The design asset cites one accepted Ontology for the active boundary and
includes or references its (P6; rc.2 #ontology-evidence): entity and
relationship inventory; invariant and cardinality law; entity-lifecycle
completeness matrix; authority matrix; atomic-function and
higher-order-function derivation matrix; governing composition and effect
algebra where applicable; whole-family Prime contraction, including every
accepted atom's admitted domain and realisation-projection mapping; and
explicit deferred, excluded and unresolved functionality.

constraints.statement: Cite one accepted Ontology and include/reference entity/relationship inventory, invariant/cardinality law, lifecycle completeness matrix, authority matrix, atomic/higher-order derivation matrix, applicable composition/effect algebra, whole-family contraction with every accepted domain and projection mapping, and explicit deferrals/exclusions/unresolved functionality. A bounded slice cites its parent and preserves parent identity, relationship, lifecycle, authority and function law; copying rows without that derivation creates a rival truth surface.

conditions: Given an accepted material-frame basis and a declared bounded action.

grounding.quote:
the
selected method basis together with the accepted design is sufficient to
recover every governing relation in the action's causally closed affected
set, and to decide whether the action preserves, changes, duplicates or
violates each of those relations. The two inputs are distinct and neither
substitutes for the other: the selected method describes which relations
are required and how to reason about them; the accepted design supplies
the concrete invariant values. A design that restates method decision law
to satisfy this rule reproduces the local-method duplication this law
exists to remove (P1, P6).

constraints.statement: Selected method basis plus accepted design must recover every governing relation in the action's causally closed affected set and support its preserve/change/duplicate/violate decision. Method supplies required relations and reasoning; design supplies concrete invariants; neither substitutes for the other and design must not duplicate method decision law. This is bounded to the declared action/set, not all future changes or reviewer performance, and adds no artifact. The law is false if a governing relation is missing or decisions require history, commentary, prior-worker memory or implementation folklore. Testing uses named cases with known governing relations and expected decisions while withholding those informal sources.
constraints.uncertainty: Material-frame and affected-set construction rules are referenced but not fully supplied.

conditions: Evaluating the action against one governing relation on its current basis.

grounding.quote:
| preserves | leaves the relation intact and operates inside it | `satisfied` |
| changes | alters the relation itself, and therefore re-enters at that relation before acceptance | `invalid_basis` |
| duplicates | establishes an equivalent path that is explicitly disposed as a constituent, replica, replacement or deliberately independent realisation | `satisfied` |
| violates | contradicts the relation, or establishes an equivalent path that is left undisposed | `falsified` |

constraints.statement: Preserves leaves the relation intact and maps to satisfied. Duplicates maps to satisfied only for an equivalent path explicitly disposed as constituent, replica, replacement or deliberately independent realisation. Changes alters the relation and maps to invalid_basis: re-entry and change at the relation's own locus precede action acceptance. Violates contradicts the relation or leaves an equivalent path undisposed and maps to falsified. Acceptance locus, not delta size, separates change from violation: accepting even an otherwise lawful change within the acting frame is a violation. Disposition, not equivalence alone, separates lawful duplication from violation. If no decision is reached, return the cause-selected core value, including indeterminate for undecidable admissible evidence and what would decide; insufficiency of method plus design falsifies the sufficiency law. A lawful change is neither a violation nor locally acceptable; a violation is not re-entry.
constraints.uncertainty: The complete external core algebra is not supplied.

conditions: For the active boundary.
exceptions: Function inputs/outputs are shown where they cross the active boundary; composition relationships where they determine boundary shape.

grounding.quote:
The standard stereotype vocabulary is `<<prime-conformant>>`,
`<<subordinate>>`, `<<effect-edge>>`, `<<deferred>>`, `<<authoritative>>`
and `<<downstream>>`. The standard visibility vocabulary is `+` public or
exported and `-` module-local or private. The standard relationship
expectations are composition for owned subordinate payloads, association
for downstream consumption, and inheritance only for real variant or
outcome families (P1).

constraints.statement: Show domain identities/cardinalities rather than helper decomposition; ownership, invariants and lawful lifecycles; boundary-crossing atomic inputs/outputs; boundary-shaping higher-order composition; IACS and Prime mappings; subordinate and effect-edge-only payloads; downstream projections; deferred outside-slice families; authority/downstream roles; public/local visibility; composition, containment, association and true variants. Standard stereotypes are <<prime-conformant>>, <<subordinate>>, <<effect-edge>>, <<deferred>>, <<authoritative>>, <<downstream>>; + means public/exported and - local/private. Expected relations are composition for owned subordinate payloads, association for downstream consumption and inheritance only for real variant/outcome families.

exceptions: A participant may be an explicitly external actor rather than a domain-model entity.
Malformed input/output, retry, recursion, fan-out/fan-in, nested workflow and human escalation paths are shown where applicable.

grounding.quote:
Every participant exists in the domain model or is an
explicitly external actor. Every message binds to a declared carrier
transform, graph or computation constructor, interpreter action or
effect-handler call; a private loop, service method, plugin, shell or
script may not silently replace a declared workflow transition. Every
message also binds to an Ontology function and its admitted authority
role; actor identity or call reachability alone does not authorise a
message (P6).

constraints.statement: Show the supported path from admitted input to result or truthful stop and owner/required authority for every decision, admission, execution, projection and effect boundary. Every participant has domain-model membership or explicit external status. Every message binds both a declared transform/constructor/interpreter/effect call and an Ontology function with admitted authority role. Private loops, services, plugins, shells and scripts cannot silently replace declared workflow transitions; identity or reachability alone cannot authorise messages.

grounding.quote:
It shows the complete admitted lifecycle for
the active boundary, including refusal, blocked, continuation, retry,
escalation and terminal states that the boundary can produce. Every
transition binds to an Ontology function and names its owning authority,
admission, compiler, interpreter, event, projection or external act.
Controller-local memory is not a lawful source of lifecycle truth when the
product declares replay, event, graph or carrier ownership (P6).

constraints.statement: Show the entire admitted active-boundary lifecycle, including producible refusal, blocked, continuation, retry, escalation and terminal states. Every transition binds an Ontology function and names its owning authority, admission, compiler, interpreter, event, projection or external act. If the Product declares replay/event/graph/carrier ownership, controller-local memory is not lawful lifecycle truth.

exceptions: Graph/compute visibility duties apply to graph-native work.

grounding.quote:
For graph-native work, every batch, retry, recursion or nested workflow is
visible through the product's declared graph or compute algebra. A
relied-on `semantic_not_realized` constructor is a blocking gap; it may
not be replaced by imperative glue in a plugin, shell, service, script or
test harness (P6, P5).

constraints.statement: Evaluate every applicable product/graph/language/runtime/handler/module axiom. Prove every view element derives from accepted Ontology; every functionality row has a derived/deferred/excluded/gap disposition; every sequence participant and lifecycle carrier exists in the domain model; every message has a declared semantic/effect boundary; every transition derives from admitted truth; every function/transition has explicit authority and composition does not widen it; every public operation projects an Ontology function; raw probabilistic output cannot directly become accepted/closed; handlers/plugins own interiors only when runtime owns admission/events/continuation/closure; native types enforce locally decidable relations; admission/semantic compilation owns global references/completeness/realisation gaps. In graph-native work all batch/retry/recursion/nested workflow is algebra-visible; relied-on semantic_not_realized constructors block and cannot be bypassed by imperative glue.
constraints.uncertainty: The participant requirement is broader in wording than the explicit external-actor exception in the Sequence model section; this tension is retained separately.

conditions: Evaluating one axiom for the active boundary on the exact Ontology and design basis.

grounding.quote:
| `pass` | the cited Ontology, view and enforcement evidence establishes that the design meets the axiom | `satisfied` |
| `not_applicable` | the axiom's applicability premise is false for the active boundary on basis-bound facts, and the reason names those facts and the authority whose scope declaration excludes the axiom ([ACTIVATION §1 Applicability](ACTIVATION.md#applicability)) | `satisfied` |
| `fail` | the axiom applies, and the evidence names an element, message, transition, authority path or enforcement that violates it; that is the counterexample | `falsified` |

constraints.statement: The mapped predicate is the disjunction 'design meets the axiom, or axiom does not apply'. pass requires cited Ontology/view/enforcement evidence and maps to satisfied. not_applicable requires a false applicability premise on basis-bound facts, naming those facts and the scope-excluding authority; it maps to satisfied only for the disjunction, never for conformance. Unresolved applicability does not support not_applicable. fail requires applicability and a named violating element/message/transition/authority path/enforcement counterexample and maps to falsified. Record verdict with value. If evaluation reaches no verdict, record cause-selected core value and what would decide: indeterminate for undecidable evidence, out_of_frame for undeclared relation/evaluator capability, invalid_basis for unsupported Ontology/design basis. An applicable axiom not evaluated has no result. Undecided and unevaluated are neither pass nor fail; exclusion is neither conformance nor failure.

conditions: A new or semantically changed boundary is proposed for promotion or design-method closure.

grounding.quote:
An axiom whose result
is not `satisfied`, whether `fail` or a core value recorded directly, an
applicable axiom with no result, or an axiom with no result whose
applicability is not established false, keeps the verdict non-accepted
as a failed axiom does, because a combination with a non-satisfied
mandatory result or a gap is never `satisfied`

constraints.statement: Both Ontology and design verdicts must be accepted before affected implementation, public contract or semantic carrier promotion or closure. Failed applicable axioms, missing functionality dispositions, unresolved authority paths and blocking realisation gaps keep acceptance unavailable. So do any non-satisfied axiom result, an applicable unevaluated axiom, or an axiom with no result whose applicability is not established false. Design authority consumes availability, decision-completeness assessment, axiom verdicts and cross-view proofs but separately decides acceptance; an all-pass matrix is evidence, never acceptance, and producing the pack establishes neither assessment nor acceptance.
constraints.uncertainty: Other disposition names/core mappings and the complete decision-completeness criterion are referenced outside the supplied text.

exceptions: An unchanged realization_refactor cites accepted Ontology/design, identifies touched projections and proves no entity/relationship/lifecycle/authority/function/effect/public-semantic delta, reusing the existing verdict without a new ceremony.

grounding.quote:
The asset stays boundary-bounded. It is a defect if it mixes an active
semantic boundary with unrelated bootstrap, test-harness, projection or
delivery shapes merely to look complete (P2). If the Ontology, any of the
three views, the cross-view evaluation or either accepted verdict is
absent, the boundary is not design-method complete. Work may continue as
provisional co-evolution only when `co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds, but
the affected boundary may not be promoted, published or closed (P6).

constraints.statement: Admissible co-evolution permits implementation before/with evidence and retention after reconciliation, but before accepted gate it is provisional: no semantic authorship, publication authority, promotion or closure. Otherwise only disposable spikes cross affected unresolved relations. Existing code may inform retrospective design; material ambiguity, contradiction or materially non-equivalent network makes decision_complete(B) false and activates the gate for that decision. Required Ontology, views and evaluation must be accepted before promotion/closure; prior authority evaluates code, and design must not be rewritten merely to rationalise unlawful code. Assets stay boundary-bounded, excluding unrelated bootstrap/harness/projection/delivery shapes added for apparent completeness. Missing Ontology, any view, evaluation or either accepted verdict means incomplete boundary, with no promotion/publication/closure.

conditions: Material realisation components and material semantic boundaries.
exceptions: Behaviour already inside an abstract declared role is ordinary variation, requiring no role-change re-entry.

grounding.quote:
Three cases are distinguished: behaviour
already inside an abstract declared role is ordinary variation; a new
operational responsibility and a new semantic or authoritative role are
each design changes, and only those two require re-entry. Use of a
component outside its declared role set does not silently establish
identity, admission, lifecycle, ordering, closure or projection truth (P6,
P3).

constraints.statement: Every material component declares semantic/operational roles; new operational responsibility or new semantic/authoritative role is a design change requiring re-entry. Composition/use preserves applicable authority, and out-of-role use silently establishes no identity/admission/lifecycle/ordering/closure/projection truth. Cross-view evaluation must establish domain and computational projections describe one system. Every material producer-consumer path identifies fact establishment, consumption, basis/invalidators, effects, retained alternatives and accumulated work, including material method/assurance operations. Component-local success cannot establish whole-path claims; different names do not establish different computational responsibilities.
constraints.uncertainty: IDENTITY §6, ACTIVATION §§4,7 and ASSURANCE §13 supply referenced supporting relations not fully included here.

conditions: Material algorithmic work.

grounding.quote:
Bind
any acceptance limits and their owning authority before qualification;
limits and workloads are Product-owned, not universal method constants.
Challenge the assumptions on representative supported paths and material
growth. Observe work directly where elapsed time cannot locate it, without
repeating the operation merely to count it. Existing design and proof
surfaces carry these relations; no additional accounting system or fixed
algorithmic complexity is required (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: Declare supported input dimensions, workload/growth and operational assumptions for the selected outcome; separate material startup, framework, external computation, transport and assurance costs under the cited law. Bind acceptance limits and their owners before qualification; limits/workloads belong to Product rather than universal method constants. Challenge assumptions on representative supported paths and material growth, directly observe work when timing cannot locate it, and do not rerun merely to count. Existing design/proof surfaces suffice; neither an extra accounting system nor a fixed complexity class is required.
constraints.uncertainty: ACTIVATION §6's detailed cost relation is not supplied.

conditions: Comparing materially repeated or similar computational components.
exceptions: Independent implementation may be justified by isolation, substrate, performance, security or dependency ownership under stated non-semantic constraints.

grounding.quote:
Two components may share a map or an append-only sequence while differing
in identity and key law, ownership, ordering, admissible mutation,
consistency and concurrency, retention, failure semantics, access policy,
lifecycle or authority over truth. A materially non-equivalent law among
those dimensions requires separation. Other differences justify separation
only when evaluation shows that parameterisation or adaptation would
weaken ownership, authority, lifecycle, failure or operational
constraints. The existence of a difference does not by itself discharge
Prime contraction or recurrence review (P3, P6).

constraints.statement: Similarity yields a commonisation candidate, then semantic/operational equivalence evaluation, then reuse, a parameterised common relation or justified separation. Materially different identity/key, ownership, ordering, mutation, consistency/concurrency, retention, failure, access, lifecycle or authority law requires separation. Other differences justify separation only if parameterisation/adaptation would weaken ownership, authority, lifecycle, failure or operational constraints; difference alone does not discharge contraction/review. Every material algorithmic obligation in M(B) gets semantic disposition (existing accepted relation, extension, new candidate) and realisation disposition (consume, local implementation, optimise, adapt, deliberate constrained duplication). Local implementation may not recast existing accepted meaning/authority as new local truth. The law is false for equivalent machinery lacking semantic disposition, generic machinery becoming authority, commonising superficially similar but materially different laws, or claiming existing accepted relations as local truth.
constraints.uncertainty: M(B)'s complete population is referenced but not supplied.

grounding.quote:
This is a theoretical justification, not an extra prerequisite. The rules
of this profile remain engineering law even where the Markov-object
construct is irrelevant, unavailable or still only candidate-class
(FOUNDATIONS §5). The framing sharpens the ask; it does not expand the
scope of the profile (P1).

constraints.statement: The engineering profile stands on its own: no adoption of world-model domain, Constraint-Emergence Ontology, empirical ontology programme or metaphysical claim is required. The analogies are IACS as smallest identity-bearing cut, promotion as independent-boundary authority, inflation as mistaking fragments for peer objects, and typing as keeping the cut explicit. Irrelevant, unavailable or candidate-class Markov constructs neither suspend engineering rules nor expand scope.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced world-model theory is not otherwise supplied.

conditions: This profile governs the realisation boundary.

grounding.quote:
When this profile governs a realisation boundary, modules should be
classified by role (P0, P6; rc.2 #6-design-module-taxonomy). Recommended
roles are:

constraints.statement: Modules should be classified by the recommended roles to bound traversal reasoning under finite context/attention/time, not for naming ceremony. Boundaries expose what is owned, consumed, emitted and sufficiently proved without rereading the whole system and expose recurrence for reuse. Design-to-module evidence, module-derived tests and lifecycle confirmation remain ASSURANCE §§14–16 law applied through the member's declared binding.
constraints.uncertainty: The detailed assurance laws and head binding are absent.

conditions: Projects use this profile.

grounding.quote:
Projects using this profile prefer one algebraic primitive plus
projections over several local decision systems, and prefer total
functions, closed enums, explicit state and deterministic folds (P2, P5,
P6; provenance rc.2 authority_compressions/stdo_compressed.md and
design_module_method.compressed.md, a claim no rc.2 body states).

constraints.statement: Prefer one algebraic primitive with projections over multiple local decision systems, and prefer total functions, closed enums, explicit state and deterministic folds. These are preferences, with compression-source provenance explicitly described as a claim not stated by an rc.2 body.
constraints.uncertainty: The cited compression sources and predecessor bodies are not supplied.

exceptions: Mutation is materially necessary.

grounding.quote:
Mutable
carrier state requires explicit justification when it is
performance-critical, required by the host runtime or framework, or
modelling a genuinely stateful boundary rather than semantic truth.
Convenience is not sufficient justification.

constraints.statement: Source truth should use typed immutable values. Preferred flow is constructor/parser to typed carrier, transform to another carrier/closed result, and read-only projection. Mutable state requires explicit justification for performance criticality, host runtime/framework necessity or a genuinely stateful boundary rather than semantic truth; convenience is insufficient.

exceptions: Totality is limited by what the language and problem allow.
Typed explicit failure is preferred when practical.

grounding.quote:
Preferred: invalid input is rejected at the boundary; semantic
kernels consume admitted carriers only; failure is returned in a typed and
explicit form when practical. Projects using this profile should prefer
`Result`-like or closed outcome carriers, explicit validation stages, and
explicit "unsupported" or "rejected" outcomes. They should avoid partial
functions that assume hidden preconditions, semantic `.get(...)` fallback
chains, and controller code that reconstructs missing truth from defaults
(P5, P6).

constraints.statement: Semantic functions should be total or as close as language/problem permit, including possible out-of-domain input. Prefer boundary rejection, admitted-carrier kernels, practical typed failure, Result-like/closed outcomes, validation stages and explicit unsupported/rejected outcomes. Avoid hidden-precondition partiality, semantic .get fallback chains and controller default-based reconstruction. Product outcome values must remain distinct from method evaluation core values.

grounding.quote:
Semantic kernels should not perform these effects while
also deciding the law. The preferred sequence: (1) admit or parse the
authoritative input; (2) transform it into a typed plan or outcome; (3)
apply effects at the edge using that plan or outcome; (4) publish
resulting events or projections downstream. If a function both decides the
semantic meaning and directly performs the write, the design should be
treated as suspect.

constraints.statement: Effects should be explicit and isolated; kernels should not decide law while performing effects. Preferred sequence is authoritative input admission/parsing, typed plan/outcome transformation, edge effect application, downstream event/projection publication. A function both deciding meaning and writing should be treated as suspect.

grounding.quote:
No controller, manager, service method, runtime loop or public wrapper
should be the hidden semantic centre of the system (P6, P1;
rc.2 #10-no-semantic-center-rule). That includes deciding meaning procedurally
in orchestration code, rebuilding truth from payload fragments,
rehydrating current law from legacy files or fallbacks, and flattening
typed meaning into ad hoc dictionary handling and `.get(...)` chains.

constraints.statement: Controllers, managers, service methods, loops and wrappers should not hide semantic law through procedural orchestration, fragment reconstruction, legacy/fallback law reconstruction or ad hoc dictionary/.get handling. Closure, identity, failure, next work and current truth should already be defined in carriers, contracts or explicit design modules.

grounding.quote:
Coupling should be reduced by dependency shape, not only by file count
(P6; rc.2 #11-coupling-rule). The preferred dependency direction is
`carriers -> semantic kernels -> effect shells -> projections`, not
`controllers -> service helpers -> mutable runtime state -> projections`.
Design is too coupled when many modules read and mutate the same object;
projections inspect implementation state to infer truth; a consumer can
silently rebuild source truth from raw artifacts; or tests pass only
because several modules still carry the same meaning. Reducing coupling
means reducing the number of places where meaning can be invented.

constraints.statement: Reduce coupling by dependency shape, not just file count. The preferred depicted direction is carriers -> semantic kernels -> effect shells -> projections, rather than controllers -> service helpers -> mutable runtime state -> projections. Shared mutation, inference of truth from implementation state, silent raw-artifact truth reconstruction and green tests dependent on duplicated meaning indicate excessive coupling. Reduction means fewer sites that can invent meaning.
constraints.uncertainty: The arrows are retained as the source's preferred depiction; import-dependency orientation is clarified differently by the functional checklist.

conditions: The boundary governs, observes, routes, audits or evaluates another actor/executor/builder/substrate.
exceptions: Strategy ownership is explicitly ratified for that boundary.
Budgets/scores/counters/heuristic assessments may belong to an explicitly owned assessment boundary.

grounding.quote:
Unlawful strategy
drift includes imperative instructions about how the downstream actor
should repair or act; framework-owned preference rules masquerading as
observability; budgets, scores, counters or heuristic ratings that
recreate the governed actor's own judgment unless that assessment boundary
is explicitly owned; and prompt, report or read-model surfaces that become
hidden strategy doctrine. Governance surfaces describe the state, boundary
and admissible routes; strategy surfaces prescribe how another actor
should do the work. A system meant to remain governance and observability
over another actor does not drift into replacement decision-engine
behaviour through contexts, projections, prompts or route helpers
(FOUNDATIONS §3 P0 boundary commitment).

constraints.statement: Publish governance truth rather than imperative strategy unless strategy is explicitly owned. Prohibited drift includes downstream repair/action instructions, framework preference disguised as observability, unowned substitute judgments through metrics/heuristics, and hidden strategy doctrine in prompts/reports/read models. A governance/observability system cannot become a replacement decision engine through contexts, projections, prompts or route helpers.

conditions: A boundary is lawfully open.

grounding.quote:
A cross-boundary opportunity discovered during lawful clean-up is not
silently absorbed into the active boundary; it is repricing input. If the
owning authority admits follow-up implementation, that work enters
separately at the smallest lawful re-entry point (SPEC_METHOD §4). This
profile owns the scope-separation rule, not the work-tracking mechanism;
for ticketed work, TICKETS governs whether admitted follow-up is recorded
and how it affects ticket closure

constraints.statement: The area should be improved subject to constitutional truth, module ownership and functional equivalence. Lawful examples include removing parser re-entry on local truth, consolidating local routes, improving a local algorithm/scan without semantic change and simplifying proof fixtures without altering claims. Cross-module lookup/index/cache/persistence repricing, public carrier/visibility/ownership changes, widened effects/observability or changed Product performance expectations require explicit design re-entry. Cross-boundary discoveries are repricing input, not automatic active work; owner-admitted follow-up enters separately at the smallest lawful point, with TICKETS owning recording/closure mechanics. Cleanup cannot conceal unauthorised redesign.
constraints.uncertainty: Referenced re-entry and ticket mechanics are not supplied.

conditions: A repeated pattern crosses more than one processed boundary; the third local rebuild triggers the stated conformance threshold.
exceptions: Third rebuild is conformant if it consumes an existing reusable surface, extends it before local implementation lands, or records an explicit do-not-commonise decision explaining continued boundary specificity.

grounding.quote:
This profile refines that rule for design review: a third local rebuild
is not design-method conformant unless the active boundary consumes an
existing reusable library or commonisation surface, extends that surface
before the local implementation lands, or review records an explicit
do-not-commonise decision and why the pattern is still boundary-specific
(P2). This section defines the design review obligation, not a rival
ticket rule or lifecycle (P6).

constraints.statement: Review repeated patterns as commonisation candidates. TICKETS §6 owns rule-of-two, third-rebuild threshold, commonisation order and migration-ticket fields library_usage, governing_library and library_rationale; this profile adds the stated design-review threshold, not a competing lifecycle. Tenant-local authority-neutral reusable patterns should be extracted. Changes to ownership, public carriers, module boundaries or common law are separate design decisions. Closure requires the selected path actually consume the accepted relation and superseded production responsibility be retired or satisfy the referenced retention relation. Compare removed work and maintained responsibilities across the path; shared names, fewer lines and unused helpers prove no contraction.

design and module assets; whether the exact claim includes every causally
applicable live requirement, accepted design relation and retained
predecessor claim; whether the exact closure claim leaves competing or
ambiguous authority on its acceptance path; whether implementation
established a material architectural decision with durable consequences
that forecloses an admitted Product outcome; and whether any discovered

through the declared ordinary assurance path; a planned or

remains open or is explicitly downgraded to the planned property

mechanical enforcement lacks its predicate or a reachable witness, if
planned evidence is reported as observed verification, if a verdict outruns
its evaluated population or declared inference relation, or if dependent
verdicts survive material counterevidence without requalification.
